questions.q: A Payables user sees a 'quantity billed exceeds quantity received' problem on an invoice. What is the MOST likely underlying cause?
options: The General Ledger period is closed
The supplier's bank account is invalid
Receiving has not yet recorded the delivery of the goods
The invoice was paid twice
questions.explain: Quantity-related matching problems are usually caused by an upstream receiving record that doesn't yet reflect what was actually delivered.

questions.q: A payment term uses the 'Days' method with a value of 30, and an invoice is dated March 1. What is the due date?
options: March 30
April 1
The 30th of whatever month the term's fixed date specifies
March 31
questions.explain: Days adds the specified number of days to the terms date: March 1 + 30 days = March 31.

questions.q: Why can two business units within the same company run Payables with different invoice tolerances?
options: They can't — tolerances are always company-wide
Because tolerances depend only on the supplier's country
Because tolerances are set per individual employee
Because tolerances and many other Payables settings are configured per business unit
questions.explain: Payables Options, including tolerances, are set at the business unit level, so BUs can legitimately differ.

questions.q: Why might a newly created supplier end up unable to be paid on its first invoice?
options: Because new suppliers can never be paid in Fusion
Because the record was saved with an incomplete profile, such as a missing site assignment or bank account
Because the supplier name contains a number
Because the invoice was dated too early
questions.explain: A supplier record can be saved before all tabs are filled in — which is exactly how gaps like a missing bank account or site assignment surface later.

questions.q: What is a supplier contact?
options: A duplicate supplier record awaiting merge
A person at the supplier's organization, such as someone who manages portal access or handles disputes
An alternate name for a supplier site
The GL account a supplier's invoices post to
questions.explain: A contact is a person, distinct from the address-level supplier site record.

questions.q: What does supplier registration allow a potential trading partner to do?
options: Immediately receive payment for any invoice
Automatically become Spend Authorized
Skip the need for any address or bank account
Submit their own company information directly, rather than having Brightfield's team enter it manually
questions.explain: Registration lets a prospective supplier self-submit information such as company details, tax ID, and addresses.

questions.q: Who issues a credit memo?
options: The supplier
The buying organization, such as Brightfield
Oracle support
The bank processing the payment
questions.explain: A credit memo comes from the supplier, telling the buyer they owe credit.

questions.q: In the Solara Packaging example with a $1,000 invoice and 8% ordinary sales tax, how much does Solara actually get paid?
questions.explain: With ordinary (non-self-assessed) transaction tax, the tax is added to the invoice total, and the supplier is paid the full $1,080.

questions.q: What happens immediately after a standard invoice header and its lines are saved?
options: The invoice is automatically paid
The invoice still needs to pass validation before it can move toward approval and payment
The supplier is automatically merged with another supplier
The invoice is automatically cancelled
questions.explain: Saving an invoice is separate from validating it — validation is still required before approval and payment can proceed.

questions.q: What happens during validation if an organization uses budgetary control and funds are insufficient?
options: The invoice is automatically cancelled
The invoice is automatically approved anyway
The supplier's bank account is deactivated
A hold is placed for insufficient funds
questions.explain: Validation reserves funds for budgetary control and places a hold when funds are not available.

questions.q: What is true about certain system holds, like a line or distribution variance hold?
options: They can be released with a simple button click, no correction needed
They automatically release after any invoice edit
They only apply to credit memos
They cannot be released manually; they are only removed by correcting the invoice and revalidating
questions.explain: Certain system holds require correcting the underlying issue and revalidating; they cannot simply be manually released.

questions.q: What technology underlies Oracle Fusion's invoice approval rules?
options: The same validation engine used for matching tolerances
A dedicated Payables-only approval database
Approval Management extensions (AMX) of Oracle SOA Suite and Oracle Human Workflow
The supplier portal
questions.explain: Invoice approval rules are built using AMX, the shared human workflow technology also used for other business documents.

questions.q: How is a prepayment entered in Oracle Fusion Payables?
options: As a note attached to a future standard invoice
As its own distinct invoice type, separate from a Standard invoice
As a line item on a purchase order
It cannot be entered -- it must be handled outside the system
questions.explain: A prepayment is created and processed as its own invoice type, with its own distribution and payment.

questions.q: How are credit memos and debit memos represented in Payables?
options: As positive-amount invoices
As negative-amount invoices
As purchase order amendments
As payment process requests
questions.explain: Both are entered as negative-amount invoices, which is how they reduce rather than add to the supplier balance.

questions.q: What is a tolerance set used for?
options: Defining how many approval levels an invoice requires
Determining which ledger an invoice posts to
Setting the supplier's payment terms
Bundling the percentage/amount limits that decide when a PO-to-invoice variance creates a hold
questions.explain: A tolerance set groups quantity and price tolerances together and is assigned at the supplier, site, or category level.

questions.q: Which scenario is a good reason to use a quick payment instead of waiting for the next Payment Process Request?
options: Paying every routine monthly invoice for the entire supplier base
Running the regular weekly payment schedule
A rush invoice that must be paid today to unblock a held shipment
Paying all suppliers on a fixed net-30 term at month end
questions.explain: Quick payments are meant for urgent, one-off situations, not routine high-volume processing.

questions.q: How is a supplier refund recorded in Payables?
options: Through a Payment Process Request, like any outbound payment
By creating a new purchase order
Through a Record Refund action that applies the received money against the credit memo or prepayment
It cannot be recorded; it must be tracked manually outside the system
questions.explain: Record Refund captures what the supplier sent back and applies it against the specific credit/prepayment balance.

questions.q: Where is the underlying Bank / Branch / Account structure actually maintained?
options: Inside Payables invoice setup
In Cash Management
In the General Ledger chart of accounts
In Procurement's supplier setup
questions.explain: Bank account setup is owned by Cash Management; Payables consumes it rather than duplicating it.

questions.q: What accounting entry does a payment typically generate?
options: Debit the accounts payable liability, credit cash/bank
Debit an expense account, credit accounts payable
No entry -- payments are not accounted separately
Debit cash, credit an expense account
questions.explain: A payment clears the previously recognized liability by debiting it and crediting the cash/bank account.

questions.q: Which of these would create a normal, temporary accrual balance rather than a problem?
options: A return-to-vendor whose original accrual entry was never reversed
A receipt tied to a purchase order that was cancelled before any invoice was ever submitted
A quantity mismatch that was never corrected
A receipt accrued this period with the invoice simply expected next period
questions.explain: A short timing gap between receiving and invoicing is expected and will clear on its own once the invoice arrives.

questions.q: What course comes next after completing Oracle Fusion Accounts Payable, according to the Financials Configuration stage of the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path?
options: Cash Management
Accounts Receivable
Fixed Assets
General Ledger
questions.explain: Accounts Receivable follows Accounts Payable in the Financials Configuration stage, covering the customer side of the same kind of transactions.
